title: Rectangular beam
spec: Create a new coordinate system with the Euler angles set to negative ninety degrees around the X-axis, zero degrees around the Y-axis, and negative ninety degrees around the Z-axis. Ensure the translation vector is set to zero, zero, zero. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face. In this sketch, create the first loop by drawing the first line from the origin (zero, zero) to (zero point seven five, zero), the second line from (zero point seven five, zero) to (zero point seven five, zero point one zero eight three), the third line from (zero point seven five, zero point one zero eight three) to (zero, zero point one zero eight three), and the fourth line from (zero, zero point one zero eight three) back to the origin. After completing the sketch, apply a scale factor of zero point seven five to the entire two-dimensional sketch. Transform the scaled sketch into three-dimensional space by rotating it using the same Euler angles and translating it using the same vector. Finally, extrude the transformed sketch along the normal direction by zero point zero one six seven units, ensuring no extrusion occurs in the opposite direction. Integrate this extruded three-dimensional model into a new solid body. The final dimensions of the rectangular beam will be zero point seven five units in length, zero point one zero eight three units in width, and zero point zero one six seven units in height.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.1083) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.1083) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.0167)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, but we can use rotate and translate methods
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The translation vector is [0, 0, 0], so no translation is needed

# Final model
r  # This will represent the final model

lanes.label: Cadabra 4B (ours) · 1 sample

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.1083) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.1083) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.0167)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90.0, 0.0, -90.0) and the translation vector is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

x_dim = 0.0167  # thickness (X)
y_dim = 0.7500  # length (Y)

# Create a simple rectangular plate

    cq.Workplane("XY")
